In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increased reaction time caused by loading memory with irrelevant items depends on the complexity of S-R mapping rules, but not on the stage structure of a task.
the increased reaction time due to memory load is not a simple function of the complexity of the task, but is a function of the complexity and the number of rules that must be held in memory.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increased reaction time resulting from loading short-term memory depends on the complexity of S-R mapping rules.
the increased reaction time caused by memory load depends on the complexity of stimulus-response (S - R) mapping rules.

The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to be aware of the potential for interference from the memory load of the task when designing a reaction-time experiment.
the increased reaction time due to memory load depends on the complexity of S-R mapping rules, not the complexity of the task structure.
the complexity of S-R mapping rules, rather than the number of stages or other task features, is a major factor in determining the memory demands of reaction-time tasks.
